title: Creamed Collard Greens with Peanut Butter and Chile
localName: Gombo vert / feuilles de chou à l’arachide
author: Pierre Thiam (SAVEUR)
desc: Collard greens boiled five minutes and pureed, then folded into a dried-shrimp, chile, onion and tomato base and finished with natural peanut butter, red palm oil and caramelised onion rings.
longDesc: Thiam’s creamed collards are a Senegalese-inspired side. The greens are boiled about 5 minutes in a little salted water, drained over a bowl reserving 1 cup of the liquid, and blended smooth. In a separate step the dried shrimp, three-quarters of the chiles, half the chopped onion and the fresh tomato are pureed; the remaining onion and tomato paste cook 6 to 8 minutes in palm oil, the shrimp mixture goes in for about 5 minutes, and off the heat the greens puree and the peanut butter are mashed in. A last garnish of onion rings, cooked about 5 minutes until soft and slightly caramelised, and the remaining chile tops the dish.
ingredients: 2 lb collard or turnip green leaves, roughly chopped (12 cups)
4 Scotch bonnet or habanero chiles, stemmed, seeded and finely chopped
1 1/2 medium yellow onions (1 roughly chopped; 1/2 sliced into 1/4-inch-thick rings)
1 vine-ripe tomato, cored, seeded and roughly chopped
4 tablespoons red palm oil or vegetable oil (2 in step 2, 2 in step 3)
2 cups water — appears only in the method
Freshly ground black pepper — quantity not printed
steps: Boil 2 cups of water in a large saucepan and season with salt (the amount is not printed). Add the greens, cover and cook about 5 minutes, until tender and wilted. Drain over a bowl, reserving 1 cup of the cooking liquid.
Blend the greens with the reserved liquid until smooth and transfer the puree to a bowl.
Clean the blender. Puree the dried shrimp, three-quarters of the chiles, half the chopped onion and the fresh tomato until smooth.

In a large saucepan over medium-high heat, warm 2 tablespoons of the palm oil. Add the remaining chopped onion and the tomato paste and cook, stirring constantly, 6 to 8 minutes, until soft and lightly caramelised.
Add the shrimp mixture, reduce the heat to medium and cook, stirring, about 5 minutes, until lightly caramelised.
Off the heat, stir in the greens puree and the peanut butter, mashing until evenly combined. Season with salt and pepper and transfer to a serving dish.

In a 10-inch skillet over high heat, warm the remaining 2 tablespoons of palm oil. Cook the onion rings, stirring, about 5 minutes, until soft and slightly caramelised. Arrange over the greens and top with the remaining chile.
chefTips: Printed cues: greens ‘tender and wilted’; base onions ‘soft and lightly caramelized’; shrimp mixture ‘lightly caramelized’; onion rings ‘soft and slightly caramelized’.
Only medium-high, medium and high heat are printed; no temperatures.
Dried shrimp are dried, not fermented, in this recipe.
commonMistakes: Leaving the greens unblended; they should be a puree.
Cooking the tomato paste on a heat too high to stir constantly.
reheating: Reheat gently with a splash of water.
healthBenefits: Greens and peanuts provide fibre, protein and iron.
culturalNote: A Pierre Thiam recipe published by SAVEUR: Senegalese-inspired rather than a traditional household formula; the page names no region or ethnic group.
sources: Title as printed: ‘Creamed Collard Greens With Peanut Butter and Chile’. Byline: Pierre Thiam. Published 16 November 2015, updated 28 March 2021 (saveur.com). Serves 6–8; total time printed 45 minutes. SINGLE-PASS.

Times: about 5 minutes (greens), 6 to 8 minutes, about 5 minutes (shrimp mixture), about 5 minutes (onion rings). The prep/cook split above (20 + 25) is a scheduling split of the printed 45-minute total; the yield of 7 is the midpoint of 6–8.
ABSENT: the amount of salt for the cooking water and for seasoning, and the amount of pepper. Water (2 cups) appears only in the method, not in the ingredient list.
